thread:
incident-bot: Pager: High error rate observed for region steering service — multiple customers reporting 503s and increased P99 latency. Auto-detect fired: cross-region-steer anomaly.
Maya (sre): I see spikes in DNS SERVFAIL and a bunch of requests suddenly pinned to ap-southeast-1 even though latency signals prefer eu-central-1.
Adrian (netops): Confirmed — steering weights flipped for eu->ap path around 3344556600. Possible policy evaluation bug.
Harper (runtime): Runtime traces show KV cache invalidations around the same time, which may have caused rapid fallback to pinned region.
Liam (eng-oncall): Paging in. I'll take lead for mitigation. @Adrian can you hold pin override controls?
Adrian (netops): On it. Preparing an emergency override to drain ap-southeast-1 for affected route.
Alex (cs): Multiple enterprise customers on eu cluster are reporting increased tail latency and 5xxs in support tickets. Asking for an ETA we can share.
Maya (sre): Quick customer impact: roughly 3% of requests hitting eu groups are being routed to ap, with P50->P99 jump and error rate ~4%. Might be a cached policy mis-eval.
Liam (eng-oncall): Running quick checks:
```
# sample probe
curl -sS -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.example/health?region=eu-central-1
```
Relaybot: Probe results show 50% of eu probes failing or returning >1.5s to ap-southeast-1.
Adrian (netops): Executing emergency routing override now: reduce steering weight to eu-central-1 and set explicit pin TTL to 30s while we triage.
Adrian (netops): Command run:
```
routectl set-weight --route /api --region eu-central-1 --weight 95
routectl set-pin --route /api --region ap-southeast-1 --ttl 30
```
Harper (runtime): Applying KV cache refresh to routing layer to flush stale evaluation results. Running patch to prevent immediate re-pin loop.
Maya (sre): Observability — enabling verbose debug on policy-eval and increasing sample rate for route decisions.
Liam (eng-oncall): On-call handoff in 15m. @Harper please own the next 30m while I patch the canary.
Harper (runtime): Ack. I'll monitor the steering metrics and DNS SERVFAIL counts.
Alex (cs): Sharing an incident note to affected customers: brief note sent, we'll update in 30m.
Maya (sre): After override, error rate dropped to ~0.8% and P99 improved. We're still seeing occasional flapping when policy service re-evaluates during cold starts.
Harper (runtime): Found a root cause candidate: race in the policy comparator where stale CDN probe results were treated as fresh; fixed in a hotpatch and pushing to canary now.
Liam (eng-oncall): Rolling the patch to canary group. Observing for 5 minutes.
Relaybot: Canary metrics: no flaps for 5m, DNS SERVFAILs down 90%.
Adrian (netops): I'll gradually restore normal steering weights over next 10 minutes once we confirm stability.
Alex (cs): Customers acknowledging reduced errors. Keeping them updated.
Maya (sre): Summary for postmortem: policy-eval race + cached probe TTLs allowed temporary mis-eval that caused mass pinning to ap region, causing increased latency and errors. Mitigations: emergency override, KV cache refresh, hotpatch to comparator, adjusted TTLs.
Liam (eng-oncall): Handoff: @Harper takes incident lead. I'll join retrospective. If instability returns ping me directly.
Harper (runtime): Taking lead — will collect logs and timeline, and file incident ticket.
incident-bot: Incident unpaged: status moved to mitigated, monitoring.
Maya (sre): Closing note: we'll set up a regression alert for rapid steering weight changes and add a canary guard in policy-eval to prevent immediate re-pinning. :memo:
Alex (cs): Thx team — customers updated, will follow up with a summary in an hour. :thumbsup:
